1887: Beside him, who knew how many answers Kiran had finished? Smiling through tears, he kept sorrowfully recounting his tragic family history. He had been born in a Queensland slum. 1892: The boy beckoned slowly, smiling faintly like an angel. Afternoon sunlight shone behind him, casting his long shadow all the way onto Lu Mingfei. Feeling he could not refuse, Lu Mingfei pushed aside his desk, approached step by step, and finally took his hand. The boy hopped lightly down and led him to the window. It was like a man and woman in a courtly dance. Lu Mingfei felt he was dancing the woman’s part; the boy controlled their rhythm.

1991: “Not much oxygen left. Is this the intended location? I don’t see the supposed ruins of White Emperor City.” She looked around. Nothing in sight resembled a city.

2065: “Not the White King. The King of Bronze and Fire, also called the Gray King. A noble first-generation dragon, one of the Four Monarchs. Norton. Born directly of the Black King Nidhogg.”
2067: “Current research says most dragons mate and have parents. First-generation dragons differ. The Four Monarchs weren’t born from male and female pairing.
